Update the guide to match and verify one database-backed legacy operation against the owned local PostgreSQL fixture without invoking a provider.
findings.title: Legacy journey selects incompatible local database driver
findings.why_it_matters: An expressly selected legacy journey cannot use the required disposable local PostgreSQL database. The launcher runs npm run dev, which forces NODE_ENV=development, while server/db.ts selects native PostgreSQL only when NODE_ENV=test; the local URL therefore reaches Neon's WebSocket driver, which expects a proxy that a regular PostgreSQL fixture does not provide. Listing and occupied-port checks stop before a database query and cannot expose this failure.
findings.validation_reason: With the newly required ordinary local PostgreSQL fixture and explicit legacy opt-in, playwright.config.ts:50 runs npm run dev, package.json:10 forces NODE_ENV=development through env-loader.cjs:6-8, and server/db.ts:45-46/73-79 therefore selects NeonPool instead of native pg; the installed Neon driver defaults wsProxy to host + /v2 while this checkout sets no local proxy, so the first database-backed journey action cannot use the fixture, and runtime incidence was not measured under the source-only review constraint.
